demos.title: Task sampling — cube count & placement
demos.desc: Fresh initial layout per seed: cube count (1-4), measured cube/cup placement on the shelf. This is where most dataset variation comes from. (No robot init-pose noise: inert for PiPER-X — see the init_pose_noise demo.)

demos.title: Action noise — default vs cranked
demos.desc: TCP-space noise proportional to the commanded delta, added to every control step; the dataset stores the CLEAN commands (DART-style recovery supervision). Same seed, two noise levels — deviation stays bounded (jitter, not drift).
demos.metrics: default: scale=0.1 pos_cap=2cm rot_cap=0.1 · 440 steps · TCP dev mean 6.1 mm / p99 39.8 mm / max 58.5 mm  |  cranked: scale=1.0 pos_cap=5cm rot_cap=0.3 · 439 steps · TCP dev mean 20.9 mm / p99 254.4 mm / max 297.5 mm

demos.title: Randomized exocentric camera
demos.desc: Spherical sampling around the workspace center with a segmentation-based visibility check — the real RandomizedExocentricCameraConfig path. Each sampled camera is drawn as a frustum with its actual rendered view on the image plane; drag to orbit, scroll to zoom.

links.label: 3D scene recording — open with: rerun random_cams_seed7.rrd

demos.title: Camera mount & FOV noise — wrist + exo
demos.desc: Per-episode jitter of the AUTHORED camera mounts (stock config, both cameras; upstream DROID-wrist / RBY1-head recipes): wrist ±4° FOV, ±1.5/0.5/1 cm, (8,4,4)° orientation; exo ±3° FOV, ±1 cm, ±4°. Complements the randomized exocentric camera above — that path re-samples the exo pose from scratch (randcam config), and its wrist cam gets this same jitter.
demos.metrics: over 200 rolls — wrist_camera: pos ≤1.7 cm · rot ≤9.1° · fov -3.9..+4.0°  |  exo_camera: pos ≤1.6 cm · rot ≤6.0° · fov -3.0..+2.9°

demos.title: Lighting randomization (randomize_lighting)
demos.desc: Per-episode perturbation of every light around its authored value: position ±0.5 m, direction ±1 rad, ambient/diffuse/specular ±0.1, random on/off (at least one light is forced back on). Same seed-5 layout in every tile; only the lighting is re-rolled. Off by default for PiPER-X cubes-in-cup — flipped on here.
demos.metrics: 2 lights · 7 rolls: 1-2 lights on · diffuse mean 0.38-0.79 · max direction tilt 48° (cap 57°)

demos.title: Texture & material randomization (randomize_textures_all)
demos.desc: One roll does all of this at once. Surfaces with a texture — floor, backdrop wall and cup body — get a random photo from a 200-image DTD subset (real messy surfaces, full hue range incl. warm; dr_texture_paths). Flat-colored surfaces (boards, cup) get rgba ±0.15 plus specular/shininess/reflectance jitter around authored values. Cubes are categorical: each independently green OR yellow per episode, gloss still jittering. Same seed-5 layout in every tile. Off by default for PiPER-X cubes-in-cup.
demos.metrics: 10 eligible visual geoms · 7 rolls: 4-7 materials re-colored per roll, 21 photo swaps (pool = 200 DTD images) · cubes categorical green|yellow

demos.title: Dynamics randomization (randomize_dynamics)
demos.desc: Each episode re-rolls physics before the robot moves, for every body with a joint — cubes, cup, all 8 robot links, and 128 invisible grasp-planner helper bodies. Mass: one ±20% factor per body. Inertia: ±20% per body per axis. Friction: every geom of an object is set to the object's AVERAGE authored sliding friction ±20% — this used to quietly strip the fingertip pads of their extra grip (authored μ=2.0 vs 1.0 elsewhere), so the pads were re-authored to μ=1.0 on 2026-07-26 after a grip test showed no slip difference (2/2 cubes in cup either way). The chart shows authored value vs the range actually sampled. Off by default for PiPER-X cubes-in-cup — flipped on here.
demos.metrics: 200 rolls · 4 cubes + cup + 8 robot links + 128 helpers · pooled ratio ranges: mass [0.800, 1.200] · inertia [0.800, 1.200] · friction [0.800, 1.200] (gripper pads: authored 1.0 → sampled [0.80, 1.20])

demos.title: Robot init-pose noise — inert for PiPER-X
demos.desc: The sampler perturbs the robot's start pose per episode (graduated per joint so the TCP stays within ~10 cm), but only if the robot config defines init_qpos_noise_range — and PiperXRobotConfig ships None (measured: stock=None), so every PiPER-X episode starts at exactly the home pose. Tiles show what the mechanism would add, using a 6-joint range derived with the documented Franka recipe (dq = w·0.1/‖J_p·w‖).
demos.metrics: stock range: None (inert) · derived range [0.029, 0.058, 0.087, 0.117, 0.146, 0.175] rad · TCP displacement over 500 draws: mean 3.3 / p95 6.6 / max 9.4 cm (budget 10 cm)

demos.title: Robot base-pose noise — ±3 cm xyz, ±15° yaw (p=0.5)
demos.desc: The sampler teleports the arm's mocap base every episode: uniform ±3 cm on each translation axis, plus ±15° yaw applied with probability 0.5 (else the base stays square). Planning is unaffected because every IK/motion-gen call re-expresses world targets (and cuRobo obstacles) in the live base frame; the exo camera is scene-fixed so the diag view does not move with the base. Grid: same layout, base re-rolled. Video: full policy episode on a sampler-noised base.
demos.metrics: sampler draw (rollout, seed 21): dx -2.7 dy -1.3 dz +1.3 cm · yaw -8.8° · base survives task.reset: True · outcome: 4/4 cubes in cup, 785 steps

demos.title: Offline re-render — simulate once, render many
demos.desc: Turns one recorded episode into several training clips with different lighting and textures, without re-running physics. Render-side changes only — moving objects, the robot, or its actions needs a real re-simulation.
demos.metrics: replay fidelity: TCP stays within 0.8 mm (mean) / 9.5 mm (max) of the recording over 262 steps · outcome preserved (recorded True → replay True) · 3 visual draws
